title: 乌鸡国辨真王
subtitle: 镜中云影与白鹤徽记
origin: 《西游记》第三十六至三十九回（低龄改编）

moral.zh: 外表和称号可以模仿，真诚的关心却藏在长期的倾听与行动里；判断真假，要找公平、可靠的证据。
moral.en: Looks and titles can be copied, but genuine care appears in years of listening and action. Fair, reliable clues help us tell what is true.

pages.zh: 师徒来到乌鸡国。太子捧着白鹤青玉令牌来迎接：“王宫里出现了两位一模一样的国王，请帮我们辨一辨！”
pages.en: The travelers reached Wuji Kingdom. The young prince welcomed them with a white-crane jade token and asked for help because two identical kings had appeared in the palace.

pages.zh: 原来，真国王被藏在一座透光的水晶井花园里。那里有台阶、花草和清泉，他身体健康，每天都把观察写成白鹤叶信。
pages.en: The true king had been hidden in a bright crystal-well garden with stairs, flowers, and a clear spring. Healthy and patient, he recorded his observations on crane-shaped leaves each day.
pages.prompt: Create the first clear three-quarter-view visual anchor for the true King of Wuji inside a safe hidden crystal-well garden with broad dry steps, flowering plants, a shallow clear spring channel, and a sunlit translucent dome. Character lock — the true King of Wuji is a kind middle-aged Chinese ruler with warm brown skin, an oval face, calm dark eyes, and a neat black beard lightly streaked with silver; he wears layered emerald-and-gold royal robes with a white-crane chest badge and a tall simple jade court crown; thoughtful, humble, never weak or frightened; child-friendly rounded proportions. pages.en: The false king wore the same emerald-and-gold robes and spoke loudly about royal business, but every polished mirror revealed a faint turquoise lion-cloud reflection.

pages.en: Tang Seng asked both kings three questions: which bridge was repaired first, which tea the old gardener preferred, and how many tail feathers the prince drew on his childhood crane.

pages.en: Joy returned to Wuji Kingdom. As the travelers departed, a red paper kite drifted from Fire-Cloud Valley with warm little sparks along its tail, inviting them toward the next adventure.
